messages:
Maria: quick heads-up — after the kernel-selection change yesterday we're seeing a ~12% drop in prefix cache hit-rate for high-concurrency cohorts. noticed during the 09:00 perf ramp.
Aj: ugh. the rollout replaced the old kernel affinity heuristic with the new latency-prioritized selector, right? could that change token ordering or kv key generation?
Chen: it shouldn't change keys by design, kernels only affect execution. but if batching windows changed, the probe cohort could hit different token alignments causing different prefix boundaries.
Lisa: do we have a repro query or short trace? can the perf bot dump a sample request/kvkey pair?
perf-bot: uploaded profile: https://perf.redwood.internal/trace/5472109876 — summary: increased first-token latency variance, prefix_cache.hits -12.3% vs baseline, kernel_selector.latency_weight increased from 0.2 -> 0.6
Maria: attaching a short example (sanitized):
```
request_id: r-9a2b
input: "System: You are a helper.\nUser: Summarize this document..."
calculated_kv_key: "pf_v2|tokv1.3|norm:sys+user|tools:sorted"
stored_kv_key: "pf_v2|tokv1.2|norm:sys+user|tools:unsorted"
```
Maria: note the tokenizer version drift (tokv1.3 vs tokv1.2) — looks like one path used the new tokenizer pin and another used a fallback. that would explain misses.
Aj: hmm tokenizer pinning is supposed to be deterministic per model version. did the kernel change cause a codepath that skips the tokenizer compatibility shim?
Chen: i dug into the selector change — we introduced an async path to reduce tail-latency. async path pulls tokenization from worker-local caches if available instead of the central tokenizer service. local caches were still at 1.2 while central is 1.3.
Lisa: so mismatch originates from local cache staleness. can we force local caches to invalidate on rollout, or canonicalize key to ignore tokenizer minor version?
Maria: discussion point: do we canonicalize to major tokenizer version only (tokv1) or include full minor? risk: ignoring minor loses exact tokenization fidelity -> possible subtle differences in model logits.
Aj: tradeoff: hit-rate improvement vs correctness. suggestion: prefer canonicalization for cache key but attach `tok_fingerprint` metadata to KV entry for safety — on cache hit, verify tokenizer_fingerprint == current, if mismatch treat as warm cache (incremental rebuild) and persist new entry. keeps correctness, allows hits in most cases.
Chen: implementation note: that'll add an extra metadata compare per lookup which is cheap (uint64). easier than full token re-run.
perf-bot: small synthetic: applying tok-major-canonicalization + fingerprint-check yields predicted hit-rate +9% on the affected cohort in simulation.
Lisa: another axis: tool/function-call fields ordering. I saw stored_kv_key used `tools:unsorted` vs `tools:sorted` — are we normalizing tool args?
Maria: current keyer uses shallow JSON stringification for `tools` field. ordering depends on call-site. we should canonicalize tool list (stable sort by name + stable-serialize args).
Aj: agreed — stable-serialize for tool payloads. also strip ephemeral metadata (nonce, request_id) from the key.
Chen: proposed quick plan:
1) immediate hotfix: force local tokenizer caches to reload from central (invalidate) and rollback async path in selector for 1 hour to recover hit-rate. owner: Chen.
2) short-term (2 days): implement major-version-only canonicalization + tok_fingerprint metadata check, stable-serialize tools, and strip ephemeral fields. owner: Aj.
3) medium-term (2 weeks): add rollout hook to zero-downtime re-pin tokenizer versions for local caches and an automated warmup backfill job that replays popular prefixes to warm new kernels. owner: Maria.
Maria: also add a quick metric: cache_key_mismatch_reason with tags {tokenizer,tools,system_prompt,tool_order} so we can see what drives misses.
perf-bot: recorded metric gaps: tokenizer-tagged misses = 58% of new misses, tool_order = 22%, system_prompt_variants = 12%, other 8%.
Lisa: nice. For warmup backfill: run cohort sampling on top-5 prefixes per model and push to new kernels with a small batch window, measure kv insertion latency to ensure we don't thrash.
Aj: regarding batching heuristics: reintroducing the async path changed the batching window alignment — we should log batch start token offsets so we can compute token-affinity (how often same prefix tokens end up in same batch). low affinity -> more cold misses.
Chen: i already instrumented batch offsets in the experiment branch, will dump a heatmap. early view shows affinity dropped from 0.78 -> 0.62 for heavy-traffic cohorts.
Maria: decision: proceed with Chen hotfix now, Aj starts canonicalization PR, Maria schedules warmup job. cross-check: do we need a tiny DB migration for tok_fingerprint metadata?
Aj: just add an optional metadata column, no blocking migration (null ok).
Lisa: tests: include a randomized fuzz of tool arg order to ensure stable-serialize yields identical keys. add unit for tokenizer fingerprint compare logic.
Maria: assigning tasks in #eng-runtime board. will monitor metric delta after hotfix. call out to oncall if hit-rate doesn't recover 5% in 30m. :alarm_clock:
Chen: starting hotfix deploy now — rolling one zone at a time. ETA 15m.
perf-bot: deploy started: deploy-5472109876-hotfix (tokenizer-cache-invalidate)
Aj: prepping canonicalization PR — will include microbenchmark: key-lookup extra cost < 200ns.
Maria: thanks team. if we get stable hit-rate improvement post-rollout let's bake canonicalization into the kernel-selector branch so future async opt-in keeps cache semantics stable.
Lisa: note for postmortem: call out implicit dependency between selector paths and deterministic keying. small non-determinism cascaded into big perf regression.
Maria: closing loop here, will post short incident summary in #incidents after metrics settle. :thumbsup:
